claim: In 2024 an estimated 20.6 million people were diagnosed with cancer and 9.8 million died from cancer worldwide, across 34 cancer types and 186 countries.
source: Sung H et al. Global cancer statistics 2024. CA Cancer J Clin. 2026.
context: GLOBOCAN / IARC / ACS estimates, not a census of every case.
limitations: Modelled estimates; registry quality varies by country.

claim: Female breast cancer accounted for about 2.43 million new cases in the 2024 GLOBOCAN estimates and remains among the most commonly diagnosed cancers in women worldwide.
source: Sung H et al. CA Cancer J Clin. 2026; IARC GLOBOCAN news release 8 July 2026.
context: Incidence, not mortality leadership (lung leads deaths).
limitations: Do not treat 2.43 million as a 2026 live count.

claim: WHO states that many cancers can be cured if detected early and treated effectively, while access to prevention, diagnosis, treatment and palliative care remains uneven.
source: World Health Organization. Cancer fact sheet.
context: Policy statement, not a CONFLUENCE result.
limitations: Cure here is disease- and stage-specific, not universal.

claim: Nigeria GLOBOCAN 2022 population profile: 127,763 new cancer cases and 79,542 cancer deaths; breast cancer 32,278 new cases, leading site among both sexes in that dataset.
source: IARC GLOBOCAN Nigeria population fact sheet (2022 estimates).
context: National modelled estimates used only as setting context.
limitations: Must not be labelled as current 2026 incidence.

claim: NCI describes triple-negative breast cancer as about 15% of breast cancers and notes that it generally grows more rapidly and is more likely to recur than other invasive subtypes.
population: People with breast cancer (NCI educational summary)
source: National Cancer Institute. Triple-negative breast cancer.
context: Descriptor for choosing TNBC as a test case, not a parameter.
limitations: Percentages vary by cohort and assay definition.

claim: Tumour heterogeneity, evolutionary dynamics, phenotypic plasticity, microenvironmental interactions and treatment resistance are interconnected processes that complicate prediction of therapeutic response.
source: Reviews in mathematical oncology and NCI tumour-heterogeneity summaries.
limitations: A review statement is not a measured coupling in confluence_v2_15d.

claim: Ordinary differential equations, stochastic models, agent-based approaches and control-theoretic methods can represent tumour growth, treatment response and resistance evolution as in-silico laboratories.
source: Altrock, Liu, Michor. The mathematics of cancer. Nat Rev Cancer. 2015.
context: Justifies modelling as a method, not CONFLUENCE efficacy.
limitations: Existence of methods is not identification of CONFLUENCE parameters.

claim: Adaptive-therapy research treats treatment as a dynamic process under evolutionary pressure rather than as an entirely fixed intervention.
population: Preclinical and selected clinical adaptive-therapy programmes
source: Gatenby RA et al. Adaptive therapy. Cancer Res. 2009.
context: Motivates control as a research layer around a frozen model.
limitations: Adaptive therapy is not a CONFLUENCE clinical protocol.

claim: PR #9 implements a read-only OnCo adapter with nine tests that refuse OnCo knowledge and the legacy gene_to_parameter_map as identified parameters, and does not modify CancerODE.
context: Methodological result: gates exist in code.

claim: The three-arm validation protocol (separate, conjoined, universality) is a hypothesis-testing programme with planned datasets and numeric thresholds; those thresholds are not demonstrated results in this repository.
time_period: protocol text on branch; timeline dates are plans
context: Keep H0/H1 explicit. Do not convert protocol numbers into findings.
limitations: No qualifying Arm 1-3 reports were treated as complete for this page.
